correctness.rationale: Endpoint-prefix nested-chain bound of 1+m(m+1)/2 auxiliary traces; two boundary marked traces already appear for distinct extremes. If a single marked interval is both extremes, there are at most 2m query traces and its open trace is itself an auxiliary trace. The marked path with auxiliary contiguous blocks attains the upper bound. Complete open-neighborhood semantics and small cases checked independently by standalone finite enumeration.

evidence: Parreau, 2013 slides pp. 15/27 and 17/27 explicitly set the VC system to closed neighborhoods N[v], bounding its dimension by two; their formula does not count open traces.
The 2026 Dreier–Mählmann–Toruńczyk definition counts N(v) intersect A but states no interval-specific polynomial.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Replacing N[v] by N(v) changes self-membership for query vertices in A; an internal vertex of an induced marked path contributes a disconnected pair of neighbours. Therefore the 2013 closed-neighborhood dimension-two theorem does not imply or contradict the open-neighborhood dimension-three theorem.
